summary: Iter 103 — Godmode onboarding QA. Backend 8/8 tests PASS. Chat RAG measured elapsed=4.54s (well under 10s target). Stripe live+configured. Register API returns 200 with token+user, sets onboarding_completed=false; POST /api/wladhub/onboarding correctly sets onboarding_completed=true; subsequent login returns user with flag=true. However, a CRITICAL FRONTEND REGRESSION blocks the entire go-live flow: on /login (and /signup), after a successful POST /api/auth/register OR /api/auth/login, the axios call resolves 200, the AuthContext login() executes (sessionStorage `wladbot_user` IS populated), but `navigate(postLoginRoute(user))` never fires — URL stays on /login and the LoginPage catch-block renders 'Keine Verbindung zum Server. Bitte prüfe deine Internetverbindung.' Reproducible for BOTH new registration (obt5-…@test.com) AND existing admin (test@test.com/test123). window.addEventListener('error'/'unhandledrejection') caught nothing; only `console.error(null)` is observed (likely PostHog SDK noise). Manual navigation to /trust proves the user IS authenticated (sidebar renders). This means: E2E onboarding UI flow could NOT be exercised via UI. Backend proves the wladhub/onboarding endpoint sets the flag as designed.

ui_bugs.issue: After successful POST /api/auth/register (200) or POST /api/auth/login (200) the try-block silently throws (caught by catch), so `navigate(postLoginRoute(user))` is NEVER called. Instead the misleading 'Keine Verbindung zum Server' banner is shown. sessionStorage `wladbot_user` IS populated by login(), and calls to /api/user/tier + /api/credits succeed, proving auth cookies+token are OK — the failure is purely between `login()` and `navigate()` on LoginPage.js lines 77-78. Impact: BLOCKS all new signups from reaching /onboarding AND blocks existing users from reaching /dashboard via the login form. Users who manually navigate to /dashboard after submitting the form CAN access the app.

integration_issues.issue: Cannot be verified end-to-end in the UI because handleSubmit never navigates. Backend behaviour verified via pytest: register endpoint returns onboarding_completed=false ✓, wladhub/onboarding sets flag=true ✓, re-login returns flag=true ✓. Frontend onboarding page itself (all 9 steps + testids) is present in code and mounts correctly when navigated to directly.

action_items: 🔴 CRITICAL BEFORE DEPLOY: Fix LoginPage.handleSubmit so that after successful api.post the code reliably calls navigate(postLoginRoute(user)). Recommended debug: (1) wrap login() in try/catch and log the error, (2) verify identifyByUser/setSentryUser/rememberLogin don't throw synchronously with the register response payload shape (backend returns {token, user:{user_id, email, name, phone, ...}}), (3) consider that PostHog.alias/identify may throw when window.posthog exists but hasn't finished init — guard with try/catch, (4) worst case, use setTimeout(()=>navigate(...),0) or await navigate before catching. `console.error(null)` was the only artefact captured — likely PostHog noise, but check `ph.alias(userId)` for the register user_id.

🟡 MEDIUM: The false 'Keine Verbindung zum Server' message on any thrown exception is a UX trap — split the catch: only show that message on `!err.response` AND `err.message === 'Network Error'` or `err.code === 'ERR_NETWORK'`; otherwise show generic error + log the real exception.
🟢 LOW: Even though NEW-USER registration hits no rate limit right now, consider a slower retry cadence for automated QA (login already limited to 10/15min per iter102).
critical_code_review_comments: LoginPage.handleSubmit catch block conflates ALL exceptions (including sync JS errors from login()/identifyByUser()/navigate()) with 'no network' — misleading and hides the real root cause. Should distinguish err.response=undefined + err.message='Network Error' vs generic throw.
AuthContext.login() has no try/catch — any throw in rememberLogin/identifyByUser/setSentryUser will propagate to the caller and be misclassified as an auth error.
postLoginRoute helper is tiny and correct; not the source of the bug.

OnboardingPage.js is 540 lines — approaching the 700-line split threshold. Consider extracting each step into its own component under /components/onboarding/steps/. The 9-step flow logic + guide messages + finish() side-effects can all live in one hook (useOnboardingFlow).

context_for_next_testing_agent: PRIMARY BLOCKER: LoginPage.handleSubmit try-block throws AFTER successful api.post but BEFORE navigate(). Reproduce: open /login → click 'Kostenlos starten' → fill any new email + password 'Onboard2026x' + phone + name → submit → observe (a) POST /api/auth/register returns 200 with {token, user}, (b) sessionStorage.wladbot_user is populated, (c) URL stays on /signup, (d) red 'Keine Verbindung zum Server' banner appears. Same repro with existing admin login (test@test.com/test123 → submit → stays on /login). Manual visit to /trust or /dashboard AFTER submit shows user IS authenticated. Once main agent fixes the navigation bug, retest the full 9-step onboarding chain — all data-testids are in place per code review of OnboardingPage.js and the wladhub/onboarding backend endpoint is verified working.
rca of the issue: Root cause NOT fully isolated in the frontend — only symptom captured. Evidence: (a) POST /api/auth/register returns 200 with valid body; (b) AuthContext.login(user) executes (sessionStorage populated); (c) subsequent authenticated calls (/api/user/tier, /api/credits) succeed → cookies+token OK; (d) LoginPage's catch block runs (banner shown) so a JS exception WAS thrown between login() and navigate(); (e) window error/unhandledrejection listeners caught nothing → the throw is synchronous inside the try. Most likely culprits: identifyByUser (PostHog alias/identify), setSentryUser (Sentry.setUser), or a stale/incompatible property access on the user payload. Recommended fix: wrap login()+navigate() calls in inner try/catch, log the actual error, and force navigate regardless. Additionally split catch block so misleading 'Keine Verbindung zum Server' only shows on genuine network errors (err.code === 'ERR_NETWORK').
